page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.large is an entry-level virtual server instance belonging to the Compute Optimized ecs.sn1ne family. It is provisioned on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyper-threading. Memory capacity is set at 4.0 GB total, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an x86_64 architecture with instruction extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. It does not include hardware GPU acceleration, bundled local storage, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate that the instance occupies entry-level performance tiers across common computing workloads. Multi-core and single-core testing yields a stress-ng multi-core score of 1457.09 and single-core score of 1098.39, while Geekbench records 923.0 in single-core and 1096.0 in multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth reaches 81.44 GB/sec for small cached reads, tapering to 10.24 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 9.37 GB/sec for uncached writes. Software compilation with Clang scores 1439.0, PassMark CPU totals 1819.34, and static web serving throughput measures 1.22 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput achieves 1.45 million operations per second, whereas small model (135M) LLM inference processes prompts at 126.21 tokens per second and generates text at 38.56 tokens per second.

Given its hardware allocation and benchmark profile, the ecs.sn1ne.large instance presents a baseline dedicated compute footprint suitable for low-intensity applications. Because it features dedicated cores rather than shared or burstable CPU credits, it provides stable resource availability. The low total memory footprint of 4.0 GB and lack of onboard storage necessitate external disk volumes for persistent storage. It is primarily suitable for non-critical development and test setups, basic proxy services, lightweight batch scripting, small Redis caching instances, and low-traffic web serving.

Networking is provisioned at a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Across synthetic benchmarks, the instance yields modest computational metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 1819.34, Geekbench multi-core score of 1096.0, and 1.45 million Redis SET operations per second. With an uncached read memory bandwidth of 10.24 GB/sec, it provides a stable entry-level compute environment suited for non-intensive workloads, including internal development environments, lightweight backend processing, low-traffic web hosting, and auxiliary utility services.
